title: Direct identification of the child through account-bound location uploads
description: By transmitting live GPS coordinates from the child's device to the backend, the child may be directly identifiable if the upload is tied to an authenticated account, device identifier, phone number, or other persistent identifier.
assumptions: Assumes the mobile app/backend can associate the GPS updates with a specific child account or device.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement; retrieved context confirms applicability of Identification for ExternalEntity->Process flows but does not provide the exact subtree.

title: Linkability of successive GPS updates in transit
description: Regular interval transmission of live GPS coordinates creates a stream of observations that can be linked together as belonging to the same child/device, enabling reconstruction of movement patterns and routines even from flow-level metadata or persistent session identifiers.
assumptions: Assumes repeated transmissions carry stable identifiers, session metadata, or are otherwise correlatable over time.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree citation is approximate; threat applicability is strong given periodic location uploads.

title: Detectability of the child's presence, movement, or routine at the backend
description: Once received, live GPS coordinates allow the backend to detect whether the child is at a particular place, has entered or left a location, or follows recurring routines such as home-school travel.
assumptions: Assumes the backend processes or stores coordinates with sufficient precision and timestamping to infer presence and movement.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is approximate; detectability clearly applies to precise live location data.

title: Disclosure of sensitive location-derived information at the backend
description: The backend's receipt and storage of live GPS coordinates can reveal sensitive personal information about the child, such as home address, school, religious attendance, medical visits, habits, and daily routines.
assumptions: Assumes the backend stores, analyzes, or makes accessible raw or derived location history.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is approximate; disclosure of information is strongly supported by the sensitivity of continuous GPS data.

title: Unawareness of continuous location collection and downstream use
description: The child and/or guardian may be unaware of how frequently GPS coordinates are uploaded, how long they are retained, what inferences are drawn from them, or with whom the location data is shared after receipt by the backend.
assumptions: Assumes notice, consent, or in-app explanations may be incomplete, unclear, or not age-appropriate.
uncertainty_note: Applies if transparency is insufficient; exact subtree id is approximate.

title: Non-compliance risk from processing a child's live location data
description: Receiving and processing continuous GPS coordinates of a child may violate data protection or child-privacy obligations if the backend lacks a valid legal basis, appropriate parental authorization, data minimization, retention limits, or adequate safeguards for children's data.
assumptions: Assumes the service is subject to child/privacy regulation and that compliance controls may be absent or insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on jurisdiction and implementation details; exact subtree id is approximate.

title: Backend stores more location data than necessary
description: The backend writes each location ping to the Location History Store, which may constitute avoidable disclosure through over-collection or over-sharing of precise location data if every ping is not strictly necessary for the service purpose.
assumptions: Location pings are personal data and may reveal sensitive movement patterns; the service may not require retention of every raw ping at full precision.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality concepts; exact subnode may differ in the canonical threat tree.

title: Location History Store retains raw location history in an unnecessarily disclosive form
description: On receipt, the data store may keep precise location pings for longer than needed or at higher granularity than necessary, increasing avoidable disclosure of users' whereabouts and routines.
assumptions: The store persists raw or highly precise location history rather than immediately aggregating, truncating, or deleting it according to necessity.
uncertainty_note: Exact retention/granularity behavior is not stated in the flow description; threat applies if the destination stores data beyond necessity.

title: Stored location history enables linking of multiple pings to the same individual
description: By receiving and storing each location ping, the destination can correlate records over time and link separate events into a longitudinal movement history for the same user or device.
assumptions: Records contain a stable user, account, device, or session identifier, or can otherwise be linked by context.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best judgement; the applicability of linking depends on whether stable identifiers or equivalent correlators are stored.

title: Precise location history can identify a user
description: A destination storing repeated location pings may be able to identify a person directly or indirectly, for example through home/work inference or association with account/device identifiers.
assumptions: Location traces are sufficiently precise or combined with identifiers or auxiliary data.
uncertainty_note: Identification may already be explicit if account identifiers are included; otherwise it may be indirect via trajectory uniqueness.

title: Location history reveals sensitive habits and patterns
description: Processing and storing each ping allows the destination to infer habits, routines, visits, and other sensitive attributes from movement patterns, making users detectable or observable within the system.
assumptions: The store or downstream consumers can query or analyze historical trajectories.
uncertainty_note: Chosen as a detectability threat by best judgement; some methodologies might classify parts of this risk under disclosure or unawareness depending on context.

title: Users may be unaware that every location ping is persisted
description: If the system stores each location ping in the history store without clear notice, users may not understand the extent, frequency, precision, or duration of location-history recording.
assumptions: Notice and UX disclosures may be incomplete or not sufficiently specific about continuous storage of raw pings.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on product transparency outside the flow itself; included because the destination's storage behavior can create a genuine unawareness risk.

title: Storage of full location history may exceed the user's consent or expected purpose
description: Persisting every location ping in the destination may go beyond the consented or expected purpose if users agreed only to real-time functionality, coarse location use, or limited retention.
assumptions: Consent or legal basis may be narrower than indefinite or fine-grained history storage.
uncertainty_note: Exact consent scope is not provided; threat applies if the legal basis or user choice does not clearly cover full history storage.

title: Backend shares more precise or frequent location data than necessary for geofence evaluation
description: P1 forwards new location pings to P2 for zone entry/exit checks. If the backend sends raw high-precision coordinates, full timestamps, device identifiers, or every ping when coarser, less frequent, or pseudonymised data would suffice, the act of sharing causes avoidable disclosure of personal location data.
assumptions: Geofence evaluation may not require exact coordinates, full history context, or directly identifying attributes on every request.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as best-fit minimality/excessive disclosure node; exact node id may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Location ping contents or metadata can identify a user in transit
description: Even if explicit identifiers are limited, the DF3 flow carries highly distinctive spatiotemporal data. Precise coordinates, timestamps, routing metadata, or stable pseudonyms on the wire can enable singling out or re-identification of the individual associated with the ping.
assumptions: The transmitted payload or transport metadata contains stable identifiers or sufficiently unique location-time patterns.
uncertainty_note: Exact identification node id is a best-fit estimate; applicability depends on payload and transport design.

title: Repeated location pings are linkable across sessions or contexts
description: Successive pings sent over DF3 may include a persistent user/device/account identifier or otherwise consistent metadata, allowing records to be linked into a movement trail. This enables correlation of visits, routines, and behaviors beyond the immediate zone-check purpose.
assumptions: A stable identifier, token, or consistent quasi-identifier accompanies multiple pings.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; core threat is strong because location traces are inherently linkable when repeated.

title: Geofencing engine can infer sensitive habits or presence patterns from received pings
description: Upon receipt, P2 processes location pings to determine zone entry/exit. That processing can also reveal broader patterns such as home/work locations, religious attendance, medical visits, or daily routines, making the user's activities detectable beyond the stated purpose.
assumptions: P2 retains or analyzes enough location history or zone semantics to derive behavioral patterns.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is an informed estimate; threat depends on whether P2 stores or enriches the incoming pings.

title: Location data may be processed for geofencing without valid consent or another proper legal basis
description: P2 receives and uses fresh location pings for zone entry/exit analysis. If users have not freely given informed consent for this specific purpose, or if another legal basis and required notices/controls are absent, the destination's processing is non-compliant.
assumptions: The system relies on consent or another regulated basis for continuous location processing.
uncertainty_note: Legal applicability depends on jurisdiction and chosen lawful basis; node id is best-fit.

title: Users may be unaware that backend location pings are forwarded for geofence analytics
description: The destination process performs zone entry/exit checks on incoming pings. If privacy notices or in-app explanations do not clearly disclose this downstream use, users may not understand that their live location is being analyzed by a separate geofencing component.
assumptions: The forwarding to P2 and its purpose are not fully transparent in user-facing notices or controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; threat depends on actual notice and UX transparency.

title: Zone definitions can link a child or family across contexts
description: The Family Account & Permissions Store shares configured geofence locations such as home, school, and friends' houses with the Geofencing & Alert Engine. This set of recurring sensitive places can act as a strong quasi-identifier and enable linking of the same child or family across sessions, services, or datasets.
assumptions: The stored zone definitions are associated with a specific child, device, or family account rather than being generic templates.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context only confirms applicability of threat types/positions, not detailed node ids.

title: Configured zones reveal identity of the child or family
description: Sharing named and precise geofence definitions such as home and school may directly or indirectly identify the child or family, especially when combined with account context or other operational data already available to the receiving process.
assumptions: Zone definitions include precise addresses, coordinates, labels, or stable identifiers tied to a family account.
uncertainty_note: Detailed threat-tree node id is approximate.

title: Zone definitions disclose sensitive private locations
description: The data read from the Family Account Store includes highly sensitive private locations and routines, such as home, school, and social contacts' residences. Disclosure of these locations exposes intimate aspects of the child's and family's private life.
assumptions: The geofence records contain actual location data or labels that clearly map to real-world places.
uncertainty_note: Detailed threat-tree node id is approximate.

title: Alert engine can infer routines and relationships from configured zones
description: Once the Geofencing & Alert Engine receives the configured zones, it can infer daily routines, social relationships, and behavioral patterns from the set of monitored places, beyond the minimum needed to trigger alerts.
assumptions: P2 stores, correlates, or otherwise processes the received zone definitions together with account or event context.
uncertainty_note: Detailed threat-tree node id is approximate.

title: Use of family location definitions for alerting may exceed user expectations
description: Family members may configure zones for safety alerts, but the receiving engine could process those locations for additional purposes such as analytics, profiling, optimization, or secondary monitoring that are not expected from the original collection context.

uncertainty_note: Detailed threat-tree node id is approximate; applicability depends on whether secondary use is possible in this design.

title: Reading sensitive family places may occur without adequate consent or choice
description: The Geofencing & Alert Engine processes sensitive location definitions about children and family-associated places. If this read and downstream processing are not covered by clear, specific consent or another valid legal basis, the flow creates a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: The system relies on consent, parental authorization, or similar privacy notices for this processing activity.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on jurisdiction and actual legal basis; tree-node id is approximate.

title: Notification reveals child's presence at a sensitive place or routine
description: By sending arrival/departure alerts, the geofencing engine discloses that the child was at a specific zone at a specific time. If the zone corresponds to home, school, clinic, place of worship, or another sensitive location, the disclosure exposes private behavioral and location information to the parent beyond what is strictly necessary.
assumptions: The configured zone may correspond to a sensitive location, and the alert contains or implies the zone identity and event time.

title: Repeated geofence alerts enable linkage of the child's movements over time
description: Even if each alert is simple, a sequence of arrival/departure notifications can be linked together to reconstruct routines, frequented places, school/home patterns, and temporal habits of the child and parent relationship.

uncertainty_note: Exact sub-node may differ in the local LINDDUN Pro tree; linkage via repeated event records clearly applies.

Zone names, account identifiers, device tokens, and timestamps can make the individuals identifiable even if the message body is brief.

description: While the alert is transmitted, its content and metadata may reveal that the child entered or exited a defined zone at a particular time. Interception, logging by intermediaries, or exposure on notification infrastructure could disclose sensitive location events.

uncertainty_note: Destination-side disclosure through storage/redisclosure is clearly applicable; exact tree-node id is approximate.

description: The recipient may not understand how precisely the child's location is inferred, how often alerts are generated, or that notifications can reveal sensitive routines and locations. This can undermine informed and privacy-respecting use of the received data.

This creates unawareness about how the child's data will be used after submission.
